title: Non-Formulary Exception Terms by Formulary (Formulary Benefit)
content:
For each formulary of the Formulary Benefit, these terms set whether a drug coded NF may be covered by exception, the tier it is covered at, and the trial and continuation standards a non-formulary exception is approved against.

| Term | Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-formulary exception may be requested | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Tier for an approved non-specialty drug | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Tier for an approved specialty drug | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| Formulary alternatives in the same class that must have been tried and failed | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Trial lookback, calendar days before the request (request date as day zero) | 180 | 180 | 365 | 365 | 365 | 365 |
| Minimum cumulative days supply that counts as a trial | 30 | 30 | 30 | 28 | 28 | 28 |
| Stable-patient continuation ground available | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| A drug coded EX can be covered through an exception | no | no | no | no | no | no |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

## Notes

- On an open formulary (Broad and Open) the non-specialty tier above, tier 3, is also the tier at which a drug that is not on the list is covered without an exception.
- The stable-patient ground lets a non-formulary exception be approved for a member who has already been stable on the drug for the lookback period, without alternative trials.

*Hypothetical reading.* Suppose a member on the Northbridge Preferred Drug List filled one formulary alternative for 28 days within the 365 days before the request. That is one qualifying trial, which meets the requirement of 1. On the Northbridge Value Formulary the same history would fall short twice over: the minimum there is 30 days, and two alternatives are required.
